* **Mentora is a keyboard-first desktop application for managing student and guardian contacts at small private tuition centres in Singapore.**
* It is designed for coordinators who manage approximately 30-200 active and prospective secondary-school students.

* It helps coordinators keep related student and guardian information together, retrieve the right contacts quickly, and maintain accurate enrolment-related records without relying on cumbersome spreadsheets or mouse-heavy systems.
* adding, updating, viewing, searching, and deleting student records;
* linking a student to one guardian while allowing siblings to share the same guardian record;
* browsing five configured subject or class groups and assigning them to students;
* displaying a student's academic level, assignments, and linked guardian; and
* saving records locally, restoring them when the application is reopened, and protecting an unreadable data file from being overwritten.
* Mentora is optimized for **fast typed commands** and clear feedback, while retaining a graphical interface for viewing student profiles and contact information.

* The MVP is intended for one coordinator using the application locally at a time. It does not manage attendance, grades, fees, payroll, accounting, lesson content, or direct messaging through WhatsApp, SMS, or email.

This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/mentora.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
This project uses GitHub Actions for CI. The necessary workflow configuration files are in `.github/workflows`. No further setup is required.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.

However, because Codecov is known to run into intermittent problems (e.g., report upload fails) due to issues on the Codecov service side, the CI is configured to pass even if the Codecov task failed. Therefore, developers are advised to check the code coverage levels periodically and take corrective actions if the coverage level falls below desired levels.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

* Checks are implemented as executable `check-*` scripts within the `.github` directory. The `run-checks.sh` script will automatically pick up and run files named as such. That is, you can add more such files if you need and the CI will do the rest.
* Check scripts should print out errors in the format `SEVERITY:FILENAME:LINE: MESSAGE`
* SEVERITY is either ERROR or WARN.
* FILENAME is the path to the file relative to the current directory.
* LINE is the line of the file where the error occurred and MESSAGE is the message explaining the error.

![UML component diagram showing UI, Logic, Model and Storage dependencies](images/ArchitectureDiagram.png)
*Figure 1. Main component dependencies. Arrows indicate use, not the direction of every data transfer. MainApp wiring and shared Commons utilities are omitted.*
| UI | Accept commands; display records, feedback and help. | `Ui` / `UiManager` |
| Logic | Parse and execute commands; coordinate saving and report failures. | `Logic` / `LogicManager` |
| Model | Maintain the in-memory register, relationships, filtered views and preferences. | `Model` / `ModelManager` |
| Storage | Load and save the register and preferences as local JSON files. | `Storage` / `StorageManager` |
The UI calls Logic and displays Model value types obtained through Logic. It does not hold a
`ModelManager` or write files. Logic depends on the Model and Storage interfaces. Storage depends on
Model types to convert between JSON and domain data; Model does not depend on Storage. The
`seedu.address.commons` package supplies shared utilities, logging, exceptions and GUI settings.
`Main` launches `MainApp`. During initialization, `MainApp` loads preferences, constructs Storage,
loads the register into Model, then creates Logic and UI with their dependencies. A missing register
uses sample data; an invalid or unreadable register uses recovery mode. On normal shutdown,
`MainApp.stop()` saves preferences. Register changes are saved during command execution, not deferred
until shutdown. MainApp wiring, Commons and JavaFX infrastructure are omitted from Figure 1 to keep
the architectural view at component level.
![Partial UI class diagram showing the manager, main window, Logic interface and student panels](images/UiClassDiagram.png)

*Figure 2. UI coordination and representative student panels. `UiPart` uses `T = Stage` for `MainWindow` and `T = Region` for the panels. The nullable associations account for initialization before `fillInnerParts()` installs the panels; other UI parts are omitted.*
`UiManager` creates `MainWindow`. `MainWindow` holds the shared `Logic` reference and coordinates
three workspaces: Students, Guardians and Groups. `UiPart<T>` loads JavaFX FXML; `T` is `Stage` for
windows and `Region` for the panels shown. The remaining UI parts follow the same inheritance
pattern and are listed here rather than repeating crossing inheritance lines in the diagram.
| `CommandBox` | Submits text through a callback to `MainWindow.executeCommand`. |
| `ResultDisplay` | Displays success or error feedback, including multiline messages. |
| `StudentListPanel`, `StudentCard`, `StudentDetailsPanel` | Show the filtered student list, rows and the selected student's profile. |
| `GuardianListPanel`, `GuardianCard`, `GuardianDetailsPanel` | Show guardians, linked-student counts and linked-student details. |
| `GroupListPanel` | Shows the current catalogue and group selection. |
| `StatusBarFooter` | Shows the data path and the session's recovery status. |
FXML layouts are in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, `MainWindow.fxml` supplies the containers
that `MainWindow.fillInnerParts()` populates. Student and guardian lists are observable; relation-only
changes also need an explicit profile refresh because they need not replace a `Student` object.
`CommandResult` carries feedback and optional UI requests. After Logic returns successfully,
`MainWindow` applies selection and workspace requests and refreshes details. On a `ParseException`
or `CommandException`, it displays the error and restores the previous student and guardian

Commands and prefixes are case-insensitive; stable ID values use uppercase `S-` or `G-` and at least
four digits. Prefix order is flexible, but a prefix cannot be repeated. Each parser rejects missing

format errors and invalid-value errors are not necessarily the same message.

*Figure 8. Parsing `assign-group sid/S-0001 g/MAT`. The incoming call is from LogicManager; `text` is the complete input and `arguments` excludes the command word. `sid` remains validated ID text, `code` is a canonical GroupCode, and `new(...)` denotes construction. Execution and persistence occur afterwards.*
Existing-record commands retain the ID as text and resolve it in the full register. Constructing a
`StudentId` or `GuardianId` advances its generator, so lookup must not instantiate an ID just to
validate user input. New-record creation generates IDs; loading existing records advances the
generators past the numeric IDs read. IDs remain stable for a record, but are not list positions,
need not be consecutive and are not guaranteed never to be reused after deletion and restart.
The generator counters are process state and are not rolled back with a register snapshot.
| Student identity | IDs are unique. Normalized name plus academic level is also unique, both on addition and editing. Phone is not part of identity. |
| Guardian identity | IDs and canonical phone numbers are unique. Guardian names may repeat. A student phone may equal any other student or guardian phone. |

| Names and search | Names retain display casing. Whitespace normalization, Unicode NFKC normalization and case folding support matching. Searches use a contiguous substring of the normalized name, not separate OR keywords. |
| Academic level | `Sec 1`–`Sec 5` or `IP 1`–`IP 6`, stored canonically. Changing level does not automatically change group assignments. |
| Phone | Eight digits starting with `3`, `6`, `8` or `9`, optionally prefixed by `+65` with zero or one following space; stored as `+65 XXXXXXXX`. |

| Guardian links | A student has zero or one guardian; a guardian may have zero or many students. Both endpoints must exist. Linking twice is rejected; replacing a guardian requires unlinking first. |

| Groups | Codes are unique case-insensitively; newly configured codes have 2–20 ASCII letters, digits or hyphens, start with a letter and end with a letter or digit. Labels contain 1–80 characters after whitespace normalization. Kind is Subject or Class. |

| Assignments | Each pair of student ID and configured group code is unique and both references must exist. A student can have zero or many assignments. Class and Subject assignments are independent; class membership does not imply subject membership. |
| Student deletion | Removes that student's record, guardian link and assignments. Keeps guardians, sibling links, other assignments and configured groups. |
| Group deletion | Rejects groups with any assigned students; an unused group can be deleted. Removing an assignment never deletes its group or student. |
`AddressBook` enforces cross-record rules even when callers bypass the command layer. Model changes
that could violate an invariant are validated before mutation. `GroupCatalogue` is immutable;
adding/deleting groups replaces it and preserves catalogue order. Saving, copying, restoring and
equality checks include the catalogue, records, guardian links and assignments.
![Sequence diagram of ModelManager delegating a guardian link to AddressBook](images/GuardianLinkSequenceDiagram.png)

*Figure 9. Successful guardian linking inside Model. The command has already validated ID syntax; AddressBook checks references and the one-guardian rule. Returns abbreviate nonempty Optional values, map operations are omitted, and Logic saves afterwards.*
`LinkGuardianCommand` resolves both records and calls `Model.linkGuardian`. `ModelManager` delegates
to `AddressBook`, which rejects an existing identical link or a different guardian for that student.
`UnlinkGuardianCommand` removes only the link and returns the removed guardian ID for feedback.
Both commands request the student's profile in the Students workspace after saving succeeds.
`EditGuardianCommand` checks for another guardian with the proposed canonical phone, then replaces
the guardian with a new immutable value having the same ID and name. Student profiles resolve the
guardian through the current register, so siblings share the updated contact. MainWindow refreshes
the selected student profile, guardian details and linked-student counts after a successful command.
**Design choice:** Store one guardian record and link by ID. Copying a guardian's phone into each
student would simplify an individual display lookup but permit inconsistent sibling contacts.
The shared record requires reference validation but makes an update apply consistently.
`AssignGroupCommand` and `UnassignGroupCommand` resolve the student in the full register and the
group in the current catalogue. They construct `GroupAssignment` from the existing student's ID
and the canonical group's code, then call `Model.addGroupAssignment` or
`Model.removeGroupAssignment`. AddressBook validates reference existence and pair membership before
changing the set. Removing the final assignment is valid; the profile then shows `No groups assigned.`
`AddGroupCommand` adds a validated group; `DeleteGroupCommand` removes only an unused group.
These commands request the Groups workspace. New Subject groups are immediately eligible for
subject filtering. Existing catalogue data is authoritative on reload, including custom groups or
**Design choice:** Reject deletion of an assigned group instead of cascading assignment removal.
This requires the coordinator to remove assignments explicitly but prevents an apparently small
catalogue change from discarding many students' tuition arrangements.
Student and guardian lists are ordered by normalized name, then numeric ID. A name search replaces
that entity's current filter. `filter-students` accepts exactly one Subject group or one academic
level, replaces the current student filter and displays its description. It rejects Class groups
and combined filters. It tests explicit Subject assignments, not the subject implied by a class
code. `list-students` and `list-guardians` reset their respective filters; filters do not alter saved
The full register remains available even when the displayed list is empty. When a successful result
requests a student hidden by the filter, `LogicManager.revealRequestedStudent` clears the student
filter after any required save. Assignment changes re-evaluate the current predicate because the
student object itself may be unchanged. MainWindow then refreshes the profile explicitly.
Workspace changes are requests in `CommandResult`, not implicit effects of every command:
| `add-student`, `edit-student`, `view-student` | Request student selection, but keep the current workspace. |
| `help`, `exit` | Open help or close the application, respectively. |
Consequently, a student command can change the underlying Students view while another workspace
remains visible. This is a current navigation limitation, not a guarantee that all commands reveal
their result automatically. Deleting the selected student clears its selection only after successful
saving; deleting another student preserves the current selection.
![Activity diagram of saving a changed register and restoring memory on a save failure](images/PersistenceActivityDiagram.png)

*Figure 10. Persistence after a mutating command executes successfully. Parsing, the recovery guard, snapshot creation and domain rejection precede this flow. Read-only commands bypass it, and disk rollback is not provided.*
1. Parse the input. Parse failures stop before command execution.
2. Execute read-only commands without saving. For a mutating command, first reject recovery mode.
3. Copy the complete register before executing the mutation. Commands reject invalid domain requests
4. Compare the resulting register with the snapshot. An unchanged result, such as setting the same
phone number, does not cause a write.
5. Save a changed register once. If saving throws `IOException`, restore the in-memory snapshot and
throw a command-specific `CommandException` retaining the original cause.
6. Only after success, reveal a requested hidden student and return the result for the UI to apply.
**Current disk-write limitation:** `FileUtil.writeToFile` writes directly to the destination.
The in-memory rollback does not undo a partial disk write and does not provide crash-safe or atomic
storage. A save error is not a guarantee that the original file is intact. Atomic replacement with
a temporary file is a required follow-up to meet NFR07 fully; it is not implemented here.
On startup there are three distinct outcomes:
| Confirmed missing path | Load two sample students and five default groups. The register file is first written after a command changes register data. |
| Valid JSON register | Load and validate all data, then permit commands and saving. |
| Unreadable or invalid register | Preserve the input file, load an empty recovery register with default groups, display the recovery error and disable register mutations and saves for the session. |
Recovery mode still permits list, find, filter, view, help and exit commands (subject to their normal
validation and whether a target exists). The footer displays `Saving disabled`. To recover, close
Mentora, preserve the problematic file, restore a valid backup or deliberately replace it, then
restart. Editing the file while Mentora remains open does not clear the latched recovery state.
Preference errors are handled separately: defaults may be used and rewritten, so the register's
preserve-on-load-failure guarantee does not apply to `preferences.json`.
**Design choice:** Snapshot the complete register for save-error rollback. This is simple and keeps
relationships and the catalogue together, at a cost proportional to register size. Per-command
inverse operations would reduce copying but would require every mutation to implement a correct
inverse. These snapshots are temporary; they do not implement user-visible undo/redo.
These are implementation gaps or release constraints, not changes to the feature specification:
* **Persistence:** partial disk writes remain possible after an I/O failure or interruption (NFR07).
Backups and restoration are manual. The ordinary `Saved locally` footer text is static, not a
per-command write acknowledgement; startup does not display the specification's loaded-record count.
* **Navigation:** several student commands preserve the current workspace even when they select a
student. Guardian detail selection has no dedicated typed `view-guardian` command. Use the current
workspace table above when testing keyboard workflows.
* **Feedback differences:** empty-value feedback can be a field-validation message instead of a
format message. Deletion reports `Student S-9999 does not exist.` for an unknown ID and confirms
guardian retention when the deleted student had a guardian link.
* **Long sessions:** assignment updates refresh filters by wrapping the previous predicate. Many
repeated updates can build a deep call chain; resetting/reapplying the filter removes the chain.
This needs a bounded refresh implementation rather than an assumption of unlimited session length.
* **Record limits:** one guardian per student; no guardian deletion, name editing, student-phone
clearing, enrolment-status field, archiving, class filtering, combined filtering, contact-list export,
spreadsheet import or user-visible undo/redo. Two students with the same normalized name and level
cannot be distinguished by the current duplicate rule.
* **Compatibility:** legacy `persons` data is ignored rather than migrated. ID generation is based on
current-process state and loaded IDs; it is not a permanent historical ID registry. Extreme numeric
suffixes are not a supported way to extend the generator.
* **Release verification:** the build targets Java 25 and bundles JavaFX 17 platform libraries for
Windows, macOS and Linux. Platform/CPU compatibility, timing, display scaling and keyboard acceptance
must be checked on the intended release package; the targets below are not claims of universal testing.
For a new command, add its command and parser, a route in `AddressBookParser`, built-in help and
tests. Mark it read-only only if it does not mutate register data. Keep reference and uniqueness
checks in the domain layer. Return UI requests through `CommandResult`; add command-specific
save-failure feedback in LogicManager when needed. For a new stored field or relationship, update
copy/reset/equality, JSON conversion, compatibility checks and round-trip tests together.

**Target user:** A coordinator at a small private tuition centre in Singapore who manages roughly
30–200 secondary-school student records and their guardian contacts, types comfortably, and works
alone with a local desktop data set. Records may describe enrolled or prospective students, but the
current model does not store that distinction as an enrolment-status field.
**Value proposition:** Keep student details, shared guardian contacts and tuition-group assignments
together, and retrieve or update them using short typed commands.
The current product manages contact and basic administrative data. It does not manage lessons,
attendance, grades, fees, payroll or accounting, send messages, or provide multi-user synchronization.
It is not intended to replace a full school-management system. Future stories below are possible
extensions, not claims that these features are available now.

This is the command contract for Mentora's first release: one Singapore tuition-centre coordinator, a local Java desktop application, and roughly 30-200 active records. It deliberately supports one guardian per student, while a guardian may be shared by many students.

Commands and prefixes are case-insensitive; the documented lower-case spelling is displayed in help. Prefixes may appear in any order, but every prefix may occur only once. Values may not be empty unless a command explicitly says otherwise. Unknown text, unknown prefixes, a missing required prefix, or a repeated prefix produces:

Leading and trailing spaces in any value are trimmed. Consecutive internal spaces in names and search queries are collapsed to one space. Therefore `Mei   Lin`, ` mei lin `, and `Mei Lin` are the same name for matching and duplicate checks. The application retains the casing supplied by the user for display, but compares names case-insensitively.

The application generates immutable identifiers (`S-0001`, `S-0002`, ... for students and `G-0001`, `G-0002`, ... for guardians). These IDs, not the current list position, are used in commands so that search results cannot cause an accidental update or deletion. An ID is an uppercase `S-` or `G-` followed by four or more digits; it is not user-editable.
| Value | Acceptable values | Error if unacceptable | Rationale |

| `NAME` | 1-80 characters after normalization; starts and ends with a Unicode letter; contains only Unicode letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, and periods between letters. | `Name must be 1-80 characters and contain letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, or periods only.` | Accommodates common Singaporean and international names (for example `Nur Aisyah`, `O'Connor`, `S. Kumar`) while rejecting numbers and accidental punctuation. |

| `ACADEMIC_LEVEL` | One of `Sec 1` through `Sec 5` or `IP 1` through `IP 6`, case-insensitive. It is stored and shown in this canonical form. | `Academic level must be Sec 1-5 or IP 1-6.` | These are the intended secondary-school levels; a closed set prevents unusable variants such as `Secondary two`. |

| `PHONE` | Either eight digits beginning with `3`, `6`, `8`, or `9`, or the same number prefixed by `+65` (with an optional single space after `+65`). It is stored as `+65 XXXXXXXX`. Hyphens, brackets, and extensions are not accepted. | `Phone number must be an 8-digit Singapore number, optionally prefixed by +65.` | The product is for Singapore centres. A canonical form makes duplicate detection and display reliable. |

| `STUDENT_ID` / `GUARDIAN_ID` | An existing generated ID with the correct prefix, for example `sid/S-0007` or `gid/G-0003`. | `Student S-0007 does not exist.` / `Guardian G-0003 does not exist.` (Use the supplied ID.) | Stable IDs make a command independent of a changing filtered list. |

| `GROUP_CODE` | An exact, case-insensitive code in the configured group catalogue. The MVP ships with subject groups `ENG`, `MAT`, `SCI`, `CHI` and class groups such as `S1-ENG-A`, `S1-MAT-A`, ..., `S5-SCI-A`; the full deployed catalogue is shown by `list-groups`. Codes are stored uppercase. | `Group CODE is not configured. Run list-groups to see available groups.` | A code is quick to type and unambiguous. Group creation is deliberately outside the MVP. |

| `QUERY` | 1-80 normalized characters that meet the `NAME` character rule; it may be a whole or partial name. | `Search query must be 1-80 characters and contain name characters only.` | Search should tolerate incomplete recollection without silently accepting arbitrary parser noise. |
- **Purpose:** Creates a student record with its generated ID, name, academic level, and optional independent student contact number. The new student initially has no guardian and no assignments.
- **Example commands:** `add-student n/Mei Lin al/Sec 2`; `add-student n/Mei Lin al/Sec 2 p/91234567`; `add-student al/IP 4 n/S. Kumar`
- **Parameters:** `n/` uses `NAME`; `al/` uses `ACADEMIC_LEVEL`; optional `p/` uses `PHONE`. Student phone is independent from any guardian phone and is not required to be unique.

- **Outputs:** Without a phone, the result panel says `Added student S-0007: Mei Lin (Sec 2).`; with a phone it says `Added student S-0007: Mei Lin (Sec 2) with phone +65 91234567.` The student list refreshes and selects the new record. On a malformed, missing, repeated, or unknown parameter, it shows the shared format error; invalid field values show their exact shared error.

- **Duplicate handling:** A student is a duplicate when normalized, case-insensitive name *and* canonical academic level are both equal to an existing student. It is rejected with `A student named Mei Lin at Sec 2 already exists.` Students with the same name at different levels are allowed, because siblings or different people can share a name; the level avoids accidentally recording the same student twice.
- **Possible errors:** If saving fails after validation, the in-memory change is rolled back and the result panel says `Could not save changes. No student was added.`
- **Purpose:** Changes only a registered student's academic level; its guardian and assignments remain unchanged.
- **Outputs:** On success: `Updated student S-0007: academic level is now Sec 3.` The profile and any visible list row refresh. Format and field-value failures use the messages above.

- **Duplicate handling:** The proposed name plus new level is checked with the same rule as Add student. A clash is rejected with `Cannot update S-0007: a student named Mei Lin at Sec 3 already exists.` This retains the no-duplicate invariant after edits.
- **Possible errors:** An unknown ID produces the exact student-not-found message. A persistence failure rolls the change back and says `Could not save changes. Student S-0007 was not updated.`
- **Purpose:** Adds or replaces the student's own contact number without changing their academic level, guardian, or assignments.
- **Parameters:** `sid/` uses `STUDENT_ID`; `p/` uses the shared `PHONE` rule. A student may share a phone number with another student or guardian.

- **Outputs:** On success: `Updated student S-0007 phone to +65 98765432.` The selected profile refreshes. An absent phone is shown as `Phone: none`; a recorded number is shown in canonical `+65 XXXXXXXX` format.
- **Duplicate handling:** Student phone does not participate in the duplicate student rule, which remains normalized name plus academic level.

- **Possible errors:** Unknown IDs use the student-not-found message; invalid phone values use the shared phone error; malformed parameters show `Invalid command format. Use: edit-student sid/STUDENT_ID al/ACADEMIC_LEVEL or edit-student sid/STUDENT_ID p/PHONE`. A save failure retains the previous record and says `Could not save changes. Student S-0007 was not updated.`
- **Purpose:** Permanently removes a student record created by mistake. If linked, only the relationship is removed; the guardian and that guardian's links to other students are retained.

- **Outputs:** On success: `Deleted student S-0007: Mei Lin. Guardian link removed; guardian G-0003 was retained.` If no guardian was linked, the final sentence is omitted. The list refreshes; an open profile closes. Parameter failures use the shared messages.
- **Duplicate handling:** Not applicable: an ID identifies exactly one student.

- **Possible errors:** A non-existent student reports the student-not-found message. A persistence failure leaves the student and relationship intact and says `Could not save changes. Student S-0007 was not deleted.`
- **Purpose:** Creates a reusable guardian contact record that may subsequently be linked to one or more students.
- **Example commands:** `add-guardian n/Anita Lim p/91234567`; `add-guardian p/+65 61234567 n/Raj Kumar`

- **Outputs:** On success: `Added guardian G-0003: Anita Lim (+65 91234567).` The guardian is available for linking immediately. Invalid, missing, repeated, and unknown parameters use the shared errors.

- **Duplicate handling:** The normalized phone number is a guardian's unique contact key. An attempted reuse is rejected with `A guardian with phone +65 91234567 already exists (G-0003). Link that guardian instead.` Guardian names alone need not be unique, because different guardians can share a name. Preventing duplicate phone contacts makes shared-family linking explicit rather than creating divergent copies.
- **Possible errors:** A save failure creates no record and says `Could not save changes. No guardian was added.`
- **Purpose:** Changes a guardian's single source of contact information; every linked student profile consequently displays the new number.

- **Outputs:** On success: `Updated guardian G-0003 phone to +65 98765432. Updated contact will appear in 2 linked student profile(s).` The currently open affected profile refreshes. Invalid values and format errors use the shared messages.

- **Duplicate handling:** The new canonical phone must not belong to another guardian. Otherwise it is rejected with `Phone +65 98765432 is already used by guardian G-0004.` This avoids silently merging two people or making a contact ambiguous.
- **Possible errors:** Unknown guardian ID reports the guardian-not-found message. A save failure leaves the old phone in place and reports `Could not save changes. Guardian G-0003 was not updated.`
- **Purpose:** Creates the student's one permitted guardian relationship. The guardian can be linked to any number of students, supporting siblings.
- **Outputs:** On success: `Linked student S-0007 (Mei Lin) to guardian G-0003 (Anita Lim, +65 91234567).` The student profile immediately shows the guardian name and number.

Repeating the same pair reports `Student S-0007 is already linked to guardian G-0003.` A student linked to a different guardian is rejected with `Student S-0007 already has guardian G-0003. Unlink it before linking another guardian.` This enforces the MVP's one-guardian limit rather than replacing a contact unexpectedly.
- **Possible errors:** Unknown student or guardian IDs use the corresponding not-found message. A save failure creates no link and says `Could not save changes. The guardian link was not created.`

Shows every registered student's ID, name and academic level, sorted by normalized name and then ID. Use it to return to the full list after a search. Guardian status is shown in the selected student's profile, not the list.
The result reports the number of students, for example `Listed 8 student(s).` If there are none, it says `No students registered.`

* `find-student n/Mei Lin` finds names containing the phrase `Mei Lin`.

Matching ignores case and uses a substring of the normalized name, so partial names work. A multiword query is one phrase, not separate alternative keywords. This command does not search guardian names, academic levels, or assignments.

The main list shows all matches. One result reports `Found 1 student matching "mei".` Multiple results report `Found N students matching "mei".`, where `N` is the number of matches. A valid query with no matches reports `No students match "mei".`

ID. Select a row to open its profile. Run `list-students` to restore all students and clear the filter summary;

Updates the shared guardian's phone while retaining their ID, name, all student links and group assignments. Every linked student profile then shows the new number, including an affected profile that is already open. The current workspace and selected student are retained.

Phones require eight digits starting with `3`, `6`, `8` or `9`, optionally prefixed by `+65` with zero or one following space. Mentora automatically saves students, guardians, groups, links and assignments after successful changes. There is no manual save command. Viewing, searching, filtering, listing and opening help do not rewrite records; neither does `exit`. Saving while a list is filtered still saves the complete register.

Your records are stored in **`data/addressbook.json`**, relative to the folder from which you launched Mentora. The location appears in the status bar. Start from the same folder each time, and use only one running copy with that data file. No account or internet connection is needed.

When you reopen Mentora, it reloads the saved register. A missing file currently loads sample students; a valid data file containing an empty register opens with no students. A zero-byte file is not a valid empty register. Previously saved groups, including an empty catalogue, are retained.

Close Mentora, then copy `data/addressbook.json` to a separate backup folder. Keep a backup before upgrading or deleting important records. To restore, close Mentora, preserve a copy of the current file, put the chosen backup at the same data-file path, and restart.

Read the command result. For example, a failed addition reports `Could not save changes. No student was added.` Mentora restores the previous records in memory, so the requested change has not taken effect there. The normal `Saved locally` footer does not override this error.

Check that the folder is writable and the drive has space. **A failed or interrupted save can leave an incomplete data file**, even though the previous records remain visible in the app. Keep backups and preserve a copy of the affected file before trying recovery. Do not treat the failed command as saved.
Mentora preserves the original file, shows empty student and guardian lists, and disables changes and saving for that session. It reports:
> Could not load local data. Your original data file was not changed; restore or replace it before saving.

An empty list in recovery does not mean your original records have been deleted. The footer says `Saving disabled`; hover over it for the failure reason. You can still list, search, filter, browse groups, open help and exit. Commands that change records, relationships or groups are blocked.
1. Copy the original `data/addressbook.json` somewhere safe before changing it.
1. Restore a known valid backup, or obtain help repairing the preserved file. Do not replace it with a blank file.
1. Restart Mentora. Saving stays disabled in the old session even if the file is repaired while it is open.
Unreadable files, damaged JSON, invalid field values or inconsistent/duplicate records can trigger recovery. Avoid manually editing your normal data file.

The MVP supports student records, one guardian per student, shared guardians, creation and safe deletion of subject/class groups, group assignments, student-name and guardian-name search, subject/level filtering, profiles, command help, and local storage for one coordinator at a time.
The following are **not included in the MVP**:
* Multiple guardians per student or editing an existing group's code, label, or kind.
* Editing student or guardian names, clearing a student's recorded phone, or deleting guardian records.
* A command to jump to an edit screen.
* Prospect-to-active conversion, active-only lists, and archiving withdrawn or graduated students.
* Class guardian contact lists and deduplicated, copyable lists for announcements.
* Importing or exporting contact lists and general incomplete-record reporting.

**Current Unicode length limits:** Some less common letters count as two characters toward the name and search-query length limit. Group labels also count some less common characters as two toward their length limit.
Mentora does not manage attendance, lesson content, grades, fees, payroll, or accounting. It does not send WhatsApp, SMS, or email messages or provide real-time collaboration between staff.

**Can siblings share a guardian?** Yes. Add the guardian once and link each student to the same guardian ID. The current guardian name and phone are shown in every linked student's profile. Use `edit-guardian` to update that shared phone number for every linked student.
**Does deleting a student delete their guardian?** No. It removes that student and their relationship, preserving the guardian and other students' links.

**Does changing academic level move the student to a new class?** No. Academic level and group assignments are independent. Use `unassign-group` to remove the old assignment and `assign-group` to add the new class.
**Why can I not delete a group?** Mentora prevents deletion while any student is assigned to the group. Remove each assignment with `unassign-group`, then run `delete-group` again.
**Can I keep a withdrawn student's record without showing it in the main list?** Archiving and active-only lists are deferred. Deletion is permanent and is not an archive operation.
**Can two guardians use the same number?** The MVP treats the normalized phone number as unique, so separate guardian records cannot share a number.
